Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service San Francisco CA
430 AM PDT Mon Sep 21 2026

...New AVIATION, MARINE, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 1201 AM PDT Mon Sep 21 2026

 - Cool conditions today

 - Warming trend resumes Tuesday, cooler again Friday into the
   weekend

&&

.SHORT TERM...
Issued at 1201 AM PDT Mon Sep 21 2026
(Today and tonight)

The local weather pattern remains dominated by a cut-off low with a 
broad rotation centered to the west of Monterey and San Luis Obispo 
Counties. The satellite imagery reveals scattered to broken high 
clouds associated with the low pressure system, some low clouds 
developing across the inland valleys, and some convective activity 
south of the Monterey County coast that has been potent enough to 
show up on the radar returns. One of those cells even lit up 
LightningCast (long story short, a satellite based algorithm for 
lightning probability) with a 50% probability of lightning but fell 
apart before reaching the southern Monterey County shore. However, 
most of them haven't corresponded to any rainfall at the surface, as 
the 00Z (5 PM PDT) sounding from Oakland revealed that the lower 
layers remain very dry. But could we still see a high based 
thunderstorm through the night? It's unlikely, even if the HRRR 
continues to hold on to K-Index values up to 22C, which would 
correspond to isolated thunderstorms, and some lightning flash 
signals near the Santa Lucia range around 4 AM to 8 AM. CAPE values 
are still the limiting factor; the 00Z OAK sounding continued to 
show a conditionally unstable layer with lapse rates around 8.5 
C/km, but this layer was still below the moist air. This is 
supported by the reflectivity values at -10 C and -20 C, which 
remain below the values that would be necessary to support the ice 
particles that would be necessary for thunderstorm development. We 
will continue to monitor the cells as they develop, because while 
the risk of lightning is very small, the chance that it would be 
accompanied by wetting rains (at least 0.1" of rain) are zero, thus 
posing an obvious concern for dry lightning-induced fire starts.

As the low moves onshore later this morning and passes through to 
our south, cool conditions will continue with highs ranging from the 
middle 70s to lower 80s in the inland valleys, the middle 60s to the 
middle 70s near the Bays, and the upper 50s to middle 60s along the 
Pacific coast. Typical diurnal onshore winds develop this afternoon 
and evening with gusts reaching 20 to 30 miles per hour through gaps 
and passes, and within the northern Salinas Valley. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
Issued at 1201 AM PDT Mon Sep 21 2026
(Tuesday through Sunday)

The cut-off low will continue to move to the east and will be out of 
our area by Tuesday morning, degrading into a shortwave trough as it 
moves into the Great Basin. This will allow more zonal flow to 
develop over the region and start a warming trend through Wednesday 
and Thursday. The word "ridge" might be a little strong for what the 
models are expecting, but there is definitely a northward bump in 
the flow that develops by Wednesday. Temperatures on Wednesday and 
Thursday will range from the middle 80s to middle 90s in the inland 
valleys to the middle 70s to middle 80s near the Bays, and the 
middle 60s to lower 70s along the Pacific coast. There are some 
pockets of Moderate HeatRisk (moderate risk for heat-related illness 
among sensitive populations) possible on those two days in favored 
interior locations, but widespread heat impacts are not expected. As 
the previous forecaster noted, Heat Advisories in late September 
typically happen with offshore flows and longer duration events. 

By Friday, another trough arrives from the eastern Pacific and 
reverses the warming trend, with temperatures closer to seasonal 
averages into the weekend. Longer-range outlooks show a slight lean 
towards temperatures warmer than seasonal averages and precipitation 
totals above seasonal averages for the last few days of September 
into the first few days of October. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 423 AM PDT Mon Sep 21 2026

Currently LIFR-MVFR. An upper-level low is bringing high clouds and 
elevated rain showers with a low probability for any thunderstorms 
to our area. Stratus on the cusp of IFR/MVFR will persist through 
late-morning before retreating to the coast. Reasonable worst case 
scenario is bayshore (OAK and SFO) and coastal (HAF and MRY) 
terminals remain MVFR all day due to an increase in onshore flow 
this afternoon as stratus would be retreating. Drizzle will be 
possible through the morning, especially at HAF and MRY, which would 
lead to further reduced ceilings/visibilities. Diurnal winds will 
prevail.

Vicinity of SFO...Currently MVFR with westerly flow. Moderate 
confidence in the overall forecast and 12Z TAF. Reasonable worst 
case scenario is MVFR stratus lingers through the TAF period with 
increasing onshore winds this afternoon. The best chances for VFR 
will be this afternoon (19Z-00Z) with an early return of MVFR 
stratus likely. Diurnal winds will prevail.

SFO Bridge Approach...The San Mateo Bridge Approach will likely be 
MVFR through at least late-morning, improving before the terminal.

Monterey Bay Terminals...Currently MVFR with southwesterly flow at 
MRY and VFR with westerly flow at SNS. High confidence in MVFR 
stratus through late-morning. As it retreats to the coast this 
afternoon, MRY will likely remain MVFR with an increase in onshore 
flow. Nonetheless, another early return of IFR-MVFR stratus is on 
tap tonight. Diurnal winds will prevail.

&&

.MARINE...
(Today through Saturday)
Issued at 423 AM PDT Mon Sep 21 2026

Moderate to fresh northwesterly breezes will prevail Monday.
Locally strong breezes across the northern waters will generate
hazardous conditions for small craft. Northwesterly breezes
increase Tuesday to become fresh to strong, bringing hazardous
conditions for small craft across the coastal waters. Conditions
begin to improve Wednesday with strong gusts likely through
Friday. Moderate seas Monday will build to become rough Tuesday
and Wednesday before subsiding to become moderate Thursday.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 423 AM PDT Mon Sep 21 2026

An upper-level low will support near to slightly below normal 
temperatures, increased diurnal winds, a deep marine layer, and a
chance for drizzle today. It is also bringing elevated rain
showers, fortunately there is a low probability for thunderstorms
as little to no rainfall is expected to reach the ground. Warming
and drying trend kicks off Tuesday with temperatures up to 10 
degrees above normal and areas of moderate HeatRisk Wednesday and
Thursday. The marine layer will compress below 1,000 feet during 
this warm-up with nocturnal drying expected above it. 

&&

.MTR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
CA...None.
PZ...Small Craft Advisory from 3 PM this afternoon to 3 PM PDT 
     Tuesday for Pt Arena to Pt Reyes 0-10 nm.

     Small Craft Advisory until 3 PM PDT Tuesday for Pt Arena to Pt 
     Reyes 10-60 NM.

&&
